Toast queue now shows one at a time (was 3 stacked). Multiple unlocks queue up and play sequentially so each gets its full animation + sound. Also added a DOM-based fallback for playback detection — if window.Events isn't available (some Jellyfin builds), a MutationObserver watches for .videoPlayerContainer appearing and triggers a poll burst. This should fix toasts not firing during video playback on setups where the Events API isn't exposed.

Fix green background on diamond spritesheet. The original CodePen spritesheet PNG had a solid green (#42AF0D) background baked into every pixel with no alpha channel. The diamond sparkle content was drawn on top of this green. When rendered on non-green rarity colors (e.g. legendary gold), the green background showed through. Fixed by processing the PNG to make all green-dominant pixels (G>100, R<120, B<80) fully transparent, preserving only the diamond sparkle content (18% of pixels). The rarity color now shows through correctly behind the diamond.

Diamond spritesheet for legendary/mythic toasts + diagnostic endpoint. Legendary and mythic unlocks now show the CodePen diamond spritesheet animation (147 frames, served from a new binary asset endpoint) instead of the trophy. The trophy is hidden for these tiers and replaced with the rotating/sparkling diamond. The client-script endpoint now also serves PNG/MP3/SVG embedded resources (not just JS). The /test endpoint now returns full injection diagnostics (WebPath, IndexFound, IndexPatched, PatchedPath, LastError, embedded resource availability) so users with enhance.js loading issues can troubleshoot.

Complete toast rewrite — carbon copy of the CodePen animation with per-rarity colors. The entire toast CSS and HTML structure has been replaced to exactly match the standalone HTML demos we built from Uenify's Xbox One Achievement CodePen. Structure: .circle (75x75 sphere gradient, pulse ring ::before/::after) containing Xbox logo + trophy SVG images (both inlined as base64), .banner-outer > .banner (355px pill with horizontal+vertical gradient, shimmer sweep, text slide). Xbox logo visible at idle, fades out at 23% as trophy fades in and rotates (rotateY). All keyframes are the exact CodePen originals (circle_grow_move, scale_circle_1, banner_animate, textSlide, rotate, shimmerSweep). Both achievement sounds inlined: regular Xbox 360 chime for common/uncommon, rare Xbox One chime for rare/epic/legendary/mythic. Per-rarity colors applied via CSS custom properties on circle + banner backgrounds.

Full CodePen-style toast port. The Xbox logo now appears inside the circle at idle and swaps to the trophy icon when the banner expands — matching the original Uenify CodePen animation we spent hours perfecting in the standalone HTML demos. Xbox fades out at 22% of the cycle, trophy fades in at 23%, trophy fades back out at 92%, Xbox returns at 93%. Trophy rotates via rotateY while visible. The Xbox SVG path is inlined directly in the toast HTML (no external dependency). Trophy starts at opacity:0 and is absolutely centered inside the circle so both icons occupy the same space and the swap is seamless.

Achievement unlock sound + richer toast visuals. The Xbox 360 achievement chime now plays when a badge unlocks (inlined as 7KB base64, respects user prefs EnableSound). Banner now has a horizontal gradient (darker edges → transparent center) layered with the existing vertical sheen, giving it noticeably more depth instead of a flat single-color fill. All six rarity base colors darkened slightly so the 'bright' shift during banner expansion (24-85% of the animation) is more visible — the color change from base to bright now reads as a real transition instead of being barely noticeable.

Fix skewed ETA calculations. ETAs were computed by dividing remaining progress by (counter / DaysWatched), where DaysWatched is the number of distinct days you actually watched something. This made ETAs wildly optimistic because it assumed you watch every day. A user who's been on Jellyfin for 365 days but only watched on 67 of them would get an ETA based on their watching-day rate (3.1/day) instead of their calendar-day rate (0.57/day), making a 4-year achievement look like it's 256 days away. Now uses calendar days since first recorded watch date (earliest entry in WatchDates) as the denominator, so ETAs reflect actual real-world pace including off-days.

Hide the header equipped-badge row on narrow phone screens. 5 equipped badges at 30px each ate ~170px of horizontal space, which on phones pushed the hamburger menu and profile icon off the right edge of the Jellyfin header bar and made them unreachable. The sidebar entry still works, so users can still get to their achievements page through the nav drawer — the header strip is now desktop / fold / tablet only. Hidden via a CSS media query (max-width: 640px) #ab-header-badges { display: none !important; } injected into <head> alongside the sidebar script. Applied to both the middleware inline fallback and the new disk-injected sidebar.js so the fix covers every client path.

Fix sidebar entry missing on the Jellyfin Android app. Previous versions relied entirely on SidebarInjectionMiddleware to rewrite index.html at runtime, but the Android app pre-fetches / caches the HTML file in a way that bypasses the ASP.NET Core middleware pipeline — so the script tags never reached it. New WebInjectionService hosted service patches index.html directly on disk at plugin startup (same approach StarTrack uses), baking three script tags before </body>: sidebar, standalone, and enhance. The on-disk patch is atomic (write-to-tmp then rename) and idempotent (marker detection). SidebarInjectionMiddleware stays registered as a fallback for setups where the web directory isn't writable, and now skips rewriting if the marker is already present to avoid double-injection. Also refreshed Pages/sidebar.js with the modern anchor-strategy that lands next to Plugin Settings — previously sidebar.js carried the legacy broken selector chain.

Hygiene pass from a full-plugin audit. Every JSON store (user badges, playback completion, audit log) now writes atomically: serialize to '<file>.tmp' then 'File.Move(..., overwrite: true)'. Previously 'File.WriteAllText' was used directly, so a process kill or power loss mid-write would truncate or corrupt the JSON file and wipe every user's unlocked badges / playback counters. File.Move is atomic on NTFS when source and target are on the same volume, which they are because the temp file is a sibling. Also fixed a StreamReader in SidebarInjectionMiddleware that was never disposed, with an explicit leaveOpen:true so the encapsulating MemoryStream 'using' still handles cleanup.

Sidebar entry is now anchored next to Jellyfin's own 'Plugin Settings' / 'Plugin Pages' item instead of wherever the first '.navMenuOption' happens to be — which, depending on which other plugins are installed, could land us inside a 3rd-party section like Kevin Tweaks. The injector walks every '.navMenuOption', text-matches 'Plugin Settings' / 'Plugin Pages', and inserts ours directly after it. Fallbacks: Home item, then first nav item (previous behaviour) as last resort.

Root-cause fix for the missing sidebar. The previous versions were injecting correctly — the problem was the script never reached the browser in the first place. SidebarInjectionMiddleware's path check only matched requests whose URL contained the literal string 'index.html', but Jellyfin web is typically served at '/web/' with no filename, so every shell-page load bypassed the middleware and no script ever got injected. The middleware now intercepts any plausible HTML GET (anything that isn't an obvious static asset, /api/, /Plugins/, /emby/, etc.) and gates on Content-Type 'text/html' before rewriting. Also fixed two adjacent bugs: (1) compressed responses (gzip/br) are now passed through untouched instead of mangled by a UTF-8 text read, and (2) Content-Length is cleared instead of being pre-set to avoid a Kestrel write race on some configurations.

Sidebar entry actually shows up now. v1.5.19's anchor strategy assumed every Jellyfin layout wraps nav items in '.navMenuSection' divs, but modern 10.11.x web flat-renders '<a class=navMenuOption>' children directly inside '.navMenuOptions' with no section wrappers, so the previous query returned nothing. The injector now finds any existing '.navMenuOption' (Home, Movies, etc.) and inserts ours as a sibling in the same parent — cloning the layout we found instead of guessing the wrapper structure. Also clones the existing item's class list so we inherit Jellyfin's exact styling. Insert position: right before the first sibling matching Sign Out / Settings / Dashboard / Manage Server, falling back to append. Retry loop extended from 15s to 60s for slow / cold-cache loads, and the MutationObserver is now throttled to 250ms so nav rebuilds don't thrash.

Two bug fixes. (1) Sidebar entry restored: the 'Achievements' link was failing to inject on themes/setups that don't expose '.mainDrawer-scrollContainer .navMenuOptions'. The injector now anchors on the parent of any '.navMenuSection' (theme-agnostic, matches every Jellyfin layout) and inserts itself as a proper navMenuSection just above the User/Sign Out section, with broader fallback selectors. (2) Toasts during playback: removed the CSS rule that hid '#ab-toast-container' whenever a video player was on screen, so unlocks earned mid-watch now actually appear, and the container is force-promoted to the top z-index layer. Polling cadence dropped from 30s to 8s, and the enhance script now binds Jellyfin's playbackstart/playbackstop/playbackprogress events to fire a poll burst within ~1s of an unlock so toasts surface near-instantly while watching.

Toast polish. Glow halos dialed way down across all tiers (was neon/blinding, now a subtle colored ring around the drop shadow). Radial sphere highlight on the circle softened. Banner sheen softened. Confetti now originates from the toast's actual position (bottom-center) instead of the top-right corner - the anchor uses the toast container's getBoundingClientRect. Banner.svg polished: one clean gold color instead of cycling through 6 rarities, slower trophy rotation (6s instead of 3s so it feels elegant not frantic), smoother spline easing on banner expand/collapse, single softer pulse ring instead of two, inner cup shadow on the trophy for depth, tighter text letter-spacing.

Big Xbox toast refinement. Circle now has a radial highlight/shadow gradient so it looks like a sphere instead of a flat disc. Banner has a vertical top-highlight to bottom-shadow sheen and an inset rim-light. Each unlock plays a diagonal shimmer sweep across the expanded banner (legendary + mythic get a second sweep). Per-rarity glow intensifies up the ladder: epic gets a stronger halo, legendary and mythic get huge multi-layer colored glows plus a drop-shadow on the trophy icon. Rarity is now applied via a class (ab-xb-{rarity}) so CSS can target each tier directly. Banner.svg stripped further - pure transparent background, no decoration, just the looping achievement animation itself (also replaces the literal '\u2013' escape bug that was rendering as text).

Xbox toast rebuilt closer to the original Adam Cosman codepen. Circle is now a solid base color with two separate pulse rings (lighter ::before + darker ::after) instead of a smooth gradient, and the circle/banner color-shifts to a brighter shade during the 24-85% expanded keyframes (mirrors the codepen's #39960C -> #42ae0e transition). Each rarity gets 4 coordinated shades (base/lighter/darker/bright). Banner has a subtle top-highlight / bottom-shadow sheen so it reads with depth without looking neon. GitHub README banner stripped of all decoration (stars, corners, rarity bar, header text) and is now just the looping Xbox achievement animation itself, cycling through all 6 rarity tiers.

Xbox-style unlock toast now uses 3-stop vertical gradients (lighter -> base -> darker) per rarity instead of flat fills, so Mythic/Legendary/Epic read with proper depth and no longer look neon and flat. Rarity color palette also realigned to the canonical rainbow used elsewhere in the plugin (#9fb3c8 / #34d399 / #60a5fa / #a78bfa / #fbbf24 / #f43f5e). GitHub README banner replaced with a looping animated SVG that literally reproduces the Xbox achievement popup: circle expands into a banner, trophy rotates inside, rarity cycles through all six tiers on a 30s master loop so visitors see every gradient.

Admin panel now has a 'Test unlock toast' section with 6 buttons (Common through Mythic) that preview the Xbox-style animation at the bottom-center without needing to play content or inject counters. Uses a new exposed window.abAchievementTestToast() helper from enhance.js. Also: new animated SVG banner for the GitHub README with a rotating gradient diamond (8s rotation, 3s pulse), pulsing radial glow, twinkling star field, and a shimmer sweep across the title.

Xbox One style unlock toast: expanding circle with rotating trophy grows into a full banner showing 'Achievement unlocked' / 'Rare achievement unlocked' + Gamerscore + badge title, then collapses back to a circle and disappears. 10.5s total animation, positioned at bottom-center. Rarity tier colors the banner. Rare/Epic/Legendary/Mythic tiers also get a glow effect + confetti timed to the banner reveal. Fix: showcase pill + header dot icons now render in white so they actually contrast with the rarity-colored border (previously icon and border were the same color). Header dots also have a subtle rarity-tinted background now.

Sidebar + header showcases now use real Material Icons matching the rest of the UI. Previously the inline injection script in SidebarInjectionMiddleware still had the old emoji iconMap fallback, so equipped badges showed up as approximated emoji (moon, alarm, etc) on the home page even though the achievements page itself had switched to material icons in v1.5.7. Also improved the visual: header dots are now 30px with a rarity-colored glow, sidebar pills use proper icon + text spacing with rarity color on both elements.

Chase modal now randomizes suggested items (different list every click) and filters properly by badge metric - movie badges get movies, series badges get series, episode badges get episodes, genre badges use Jellyfin's genre filter. 35 new badges across Prestige (15/25/50), Score Economy (500k/1M lifetime), Morning Ritual, Combo Master, Library Completionist, Badge Hoarder, Director Devotee, 7 Decade specialists (60s-20s), 7 Day-of-Week specialists (Mon-Sun), Binge Marathon (5/10/15h in one day), Library Specialist (100/500 items in one library), Actor devotee extremes, Ultra Movie Marathon, Binge Everest. New metrics: LifetimeScore, BestComboCount, LibrariesAt100Percent, BadgesUnlockedPercent, DecadeItemsWatched, DayOfWeekItemsWatched, MaxLibraryItemCount, MaxMinutesInSingleDay. New counters tracked on every playback: decade dict, day-of-week dict, minutes-by-date dict.

Pinned badges replace Smart Goals as the 'Working on' row (show only what you pick, no unrealistic auto-suggestions). Rarity-colored borders on every badge card - the whole grid now color-codes visually. Leaderboard Score sub-tab auto-loads when you open the Leaderboard tab (no more clicking between tabs to trigger it). 25 new badge definitions: 11 genre specialists (Horror, Comedy, Drama, Action, Sci-Fi, Animation, Documentary, Crime, Romance, Thriller, Fantasy), 3 streak extremes (200/365/500 days), 2 late-night extremes (500/1000 sessions), 2 rewatch extremes (100/500), 2 total-time extremes (2000/5000 hours), Year Rounder (365 days), and 4 Prestige tier badges (reach prestige 1/3/5/10) using a new PrestigeLevel metric.

Heatmap + streak calendar reworked as CSS grid with aspect-ratio:1 so cells stay perfectly square at every range. Wrapped tab redesigned with a huge gradient hero banner showing the year total, then 3 labelled sections (Your numbers / Your highlights / Your favorites) with accent-bordered cards, emoji icons, hover-lift and list cards for top genres/directors/actors. Smart Goals row on My Badges tab showing 3-5 daily suggestions tied to your closest badges, click to open the chase modal. Co-watch detection: when two users watch the same item within an hour, both get +20 score bank bonus. Compare history: last 10 comparisons saved per user with quick-access pills. Per-user notification preferences (toasts, milestone toasts, confetti, activity feed visibility, co-watch bonus opt-in) controlled from the Stats tab and honored by enhance.js.

Pin button moved to footer (no longer overlaps points chip), restyled with subtle blue accent when active and a 'PINNED' label corner badge on pinned cards. Streak calendar now has a fire-themed header showing current streak, best streak, and active days with an animated flame and gradient typography. Hero banner shows a current-streak chip when you have a streak going. Profile card adds a current streak stat. Achievement ETA: backend computes per-badge days-remaining-to-unlock from your viewing velocity (current/days_active * remaining), displayed as an orange chip on locked badge cards. Yearly Wrapped tab: Spotify-style stat cards for any past year showing items / movies / episodes / active days / best streak / hours plus top genres / director / actor / biggest day / top month / top day-of-week, with a year selector.

Big polish + skipped-features pass. Compare row layout fixed: values on outer edges, bars meeting at center label, winner highlighted green. Activity feed now paginated (20 per page) with user filter dropdown (All / specific user). Recent unlocks panel removed from Stats tab (duplicated by Activity). Streak calendar - full year SVG grid showing every day you watched. Material Icons font replaces emoji iconMap for ALL badge icons - real movie/tv/dark_mode/etc icons rendered cleanly. Achievement milestones: 25/50/75/100% catalog completion fires a special gold milestone toast with triple confetti burst. Expanded nav container selectors to match more Jellyfin themes. Added server-side logging to the middleware so we can confirm if it's even firing for /web/index.html requests.

Security fix + massive feature set. SECURITY: every admin endpoint now requires RequiresElevation policy so regular users can no longer change plugin config. AniLiberty STRM 2.0.0.15 — Jellyfin 12

### Changes

- Added support for Jellyfin 12.
- Reduced unnecessary artwork downloads during library updates.
- Reduced background processing for intro and outro skipping.
- Fixed a problem that could remove generated library files when AniLiberty returned incomplete data.

### Upgrade Notes

Restart Jellyfin after updating. No settings changes or library regeneration are required.

AniLiberty STRM 2.0.0.14 — Jellyfin 10.11

### Changes

- Reduced unnecessary artwork downloads during library updates.
- Reduced background processing for intro and outro skipping.
- Fixed a problem that could remove generated library files when AniLiberty returned incomplete data.

### Upgrade Notes

Restart Jellyfin after updating. No settings changes or library regeneration are required.

Release 2.0.0.13
AniLiberty STRM Performance Update

This update makes library generation and Skip Intro/Outro processing faster and lighter on Jellyfin, especially for larger libraries.

### Performance Improvements
- Faster full-catalog and Favorites library generation.
- Reduced CPU and memory usage during generation and library updates.
- Faster preparation of native Skip Intro/Outro data after Jellyfin starts or scans a library.
- Improved performance during repeated scheduled runs and when multiple library locations are configured.
- Reduced memory usage while processing artwork and plugin-managed library data.

### Upgrade Notes
- Restart Jellyfin after installing the update.
- No settings changes or library regeneration are required.

GitHub Release: https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin/releases/tag/v2.0.0.13
Full changelog: https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin/blob/aniLiberty-v2/CHANGELOG.md

Release 2.0.0.12
AniLiberty STRM Native Media Segments & Docker Playback Hardening

This release improves Jellyfin-native skip controls, managed-library refresh behavior, authentication visibility, and Docker playback safety. It also expands automated coverage and adds formatting/analyzer checks to both stable and nightly release pipelines.

### Licensing and Branding
- The repository is now licensed for non-commercial use under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0**.
- Added explicit commercial licensing, trademark, and required-notice documents.
- Commercial use requires separate permission from the project owner; the AniLiberty STRM name and branding are not granted for unrestricted reuse.

### Docker Direct Play Guard
- Fixed automatic playback proxy URL selection inside Docker and other containers.
- The plugin no longer writes container-only bridge addresses such as `172.17.x.x` into generated `.strm` files.
- Proxy base URL priority is now: explicit **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL**, `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl`, then native-host auto-detection outside containers.
- When no client-reachable HTTP(S) base URL exists in a container, generation safely falls back to direct AniLiberty HLS URLs and records a clear task warning.
- Invalid manual or published proxy URLs are ignored instead of producing broken playback links.

### Native Skip Intro / Outro
- Replaced generated EDL and chapter XML skip files with a Jellyfin `IMediaSegmentProvider` implementation.
- Opening and ending timings are stored in `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/media-segments.json` and exposed as native Jellyfin media segments.
- Added background warm-up and path-to-episode reconciliation so existing library items receive updated skip timings without rewriting user-authored metadata.

### Managed Mirror and Metadata Refresh
- Expanded managed manifest tracking for STRM, NFO, artwork, popularity metadata, and media-segment state.
- Generated metadata is refreshed when the upstream AniLiberty signal changes while unmarked user-authored files remain protected.
- Cleanup remains bounded to plugin-managed files, with `Keep`, `DryRun`, and opt-in `Delete` behavior.
- Improved specials, franchise-season, fractional-ordinal, hydration, and image-handling paths.

### Popularity and Authentication Visibility
- Added an optional AniLiberty popularity badge to Jellyfin Web item pages.
- Added a public, read-only metadata endpoint backed only by plugin-generated popularity sidecars.
- Added Jellyfin activity notifications when a stored AniLiberty token starts returning HTTP 401/403, with cooldown protection against notification spam.
- Improved login/password, OTP, favorites, and watch-timecode API handling and validation.

### Playback and Sync Reliability
- Kept HLS playlist and segment delivery streaming through Jellyfin without buffering complete media objects in memory.
- Improved STRM URL normalization, playlist route handling, redirect validation, and playback diagnostics.
- Improved per-session watch-progress coordination, cancellation, path resolution, and forward-only progress updates.

### Quality Gates and Verification
- Added `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` to stable and nightly workflows, covering formatting and built-in Roslyn analyzer diagnostics without an extra linter dependency.
- Expanded automated coverage across controllers, API clients, scheduled tasks, managed cleanup, native media segments, popularity injection, authentication notifications, and Docker proxy URL selection.
- Full release-gated result: **207/207 non-integration tests passed**, clean Debug and Release builds, and zero compiler warnings. Three opt-in live AniLiberty API checks remain outside the release gate.
- Reproduced the Docker failure on Jellyfin 10.11.11: an internal bridge URL caused `DirectPlayError` and ffmpeg fallback; a client-reachable proxy URL played the same H.264/AAC stream through Direct Play with no transcoding.

### Upgrade Notes
- Restart Jellyfin after installing the update.
- Run **Generate AniLiberty STRM library** again so existing `.strm` files and managed state receive the new routing and metadata behavior.
- Docker users who want Jellyfin-proxied playback should set **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL** or `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl` to an address reachable by playback devices and the Jellyfin container.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build.
- No full-segment server-side cache or mid-segment resume; brief client-side HLS buffering remains the current protection against connection jitter.
- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts or the legacy GitHub Pages repository URL.
- No season-gap fix: the reported missing-season case was not established as a plugin defect in this work.

GitHub Release: https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin/releases/tag/v2.0.0.12
Full changelog: https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin/blob/aniLiberty-v2/CHANGELOG.md

Release 2.0.0.11
AniLiberty STRM Support Trace & Docker Preflight

This update adds a safer diagnostics flow for Docker and headless Jellyfin setups: compact logs stay readable, while the Support Trace rail captures the full failure context needed for issue triage.

### Diagnostic Command Center
- Added a **Huge trace** switch for explicit support sessions.
- `Show logs` now remains the compact operational view for normal task results.
- `Show support trace` exposes the high-volume diagnostic stream only after Huge trace is enabled and the task is rerun.
- `Copy support bundle` packages sanitized configuration, compact logs, and captured support trace without exposing AniLiberty tokens.

### Full Exception Visibility
- Support trace now records full exception details, including stack traces and inner exceptions.
- Compact logs keep short, readable error summaries so normal UI logging does not turn into a wall of text.
- Verified with a read-only Docker output path: the trace captures the filesystem failure, plugin preflight stack, task failure stack, and remediation hint.

### Docker Output Flight Check
- Scheduled generation now validates that the configured output root is writable before fetching AniLiberty catalog data.
- Permission and path failures now stop early with a clear message about Docker volume mapping, host directory ownership, and PUID/PGID permissions.
- Favorites and full-catalog generation both run this preflight before network/catalog work begins.

### Noise Suppression
- Detailed catalog page progress, per-title generation chatter, and stale-file dry-run lists are routed into support trace instead of compact logs.
- Compact logging defaults remain tuned for routine operation.
- Debug logging in compact logs is now described separately from support trace so the UI makes the diagnostic path clearer.

### Verification
- Built and tested with the non-integration suite.
- Smoke-tested in Docker on Jellyfin 10.11 with manifest installation.
- Confirmed support trace captures full write-permission failures while compact logs remain short.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build.
- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.
- No change to the legacy repository URL used for the plugin manifest.

GitHub Release: https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin/releases/tag/v2.0.0.11
Full changelog: https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin/blob/aniLiberty-v2/CHANGELOG.md

Release 2.0.0.10
AniLiberty STRM Docker Playback Rail Fix

This update tightens the Docker playback path for AniLiberty STRM Plugin and documents the supported container workflow: repository manifest install, container-visible output path, scheduled reconstruction, Jellyfin library scan, and proxied HLS playback.

### Docker Playback Proxy Rail
- Fixed a Docker/headless Jellyfin case where `ReverseVirtualPath` could resolve the playback proxy route as `file:///AniLibertyPlayback/hls`.
- Generated `.strm` files now keep the Playback Proxy Rail on HTTP/HTTPS instead of writing unusable `file://` proxy URLs.
- Added proxy endpoint tests that preserve valid absolute HTTP routes and normalize non-HTTP absolute routes back into Jellyfin route paths.

### Docker First Launch Flight Check
- Added a README path contract for Docker: plugin output path and Jellyfin media library path must use the same container-visible path.
- Documented a working volume pattern such as `/srv/aniliberty-strm:/media/aniliberty-strm`.
- Added a first-run sequence for full-catalog generation, favorites generation, scheduled tasks, and empty-output diagnostics.

### Tested Environment
- Verified manifest-based installation in Docker using `jellyfin/jellyfin:10.11.0`.
- Smoke-tested on Windows 10 Pro with Docker Desktop 4.51.0, Docker Engine 28.5.2, and Docker Compose 2.40.3.
- Confirmed Jellyfin scans generated output as a TV library, recognizes generated series and episodes, returns item-level playback info, rewrites HLS playlists through the proxy, and streams HLS segments through the plugin route.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build.
- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.

Release 2.0.0.9
AniLiberty STRM Hardening System Release

This update hardens AniLiberty STRM Plugin as a full Jellyfin reconstruction system: stable Jellyfin ABI targeting, explicit AniLiberty identity, safer generated-library governance, streaming playback proxying, and a stronger operational surface for administrators.

### Jellyfin Compatibility & Quality Gates
- Pinned all `Jellyfin.*` NuGet references to `10.11.0` to stop builds from silently drifting to newer Jellyfin packages.
- Added committed `packages.lock.json` files and locked restore in CI.
- Added CI checks that verify every resolved `Jellyfin.*` package remains on `10.11.0` while `targetAbi` stays `10.11.0.0`.
- Release automation now keeps `build.yaml`, package version, assembly version, file version, and informational version in sync.

### AniLiberty Identity & API Courtesy
- Rebranded the public plugin identity to **AniLiberty STRM Plugin** while keeping the legacy `AniLibriaStrmPlugin` repository URL for install compatibility and branch history.
- Added a shared `PluginIdentity` with display name, product token, repository URL, version discovery, and canonical User-Agent.
- All AniLiberty API, media proxy, static media, and HLS clients now identify as:
  `AniLibertyStrmPlugin/<version> (Jellyfin; +https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin)`.

### Mirror Governance Layer
- Added `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/manifest.json` inside each output root to track files managed by the plugin.
- The manifest records generated STRM, ANIID, EDL, chapter XML, NFO, artwork/thumbs, release/episode IDs, hashes, sources, and timestamps.
- First manifest run initializes the baseline and never prunes existing files.
- Generated NFO/artwork refreshes only when the file is known as plugin-managed through the manifest or generated marker.
- Existing unmarked `.nfo` files and artwork are preserved as user-owned content.

### Safe Cleanup Modes
- Added `StaleCleanupMode`: `Off`, `DryRun`, and `Delete`.
- Default is `DryRun`, which reports stale managed files without deleting anything.
- `Delete` removes only manifest-managed stale files and then removes empty directories created by that cleanup path.
- Untracked user files are left alone.

### Playback Proxy Rail
- Non-playlist HLS segments and keys now stream directly to `Response.Body`.
- The proxy no longer reads segment/key payloads into memory with `ReadAsByteArrayAsync`.
- Upstream host allow-listing and redirect validation remain in place.
- Playlist rewriting continues to route segments and keys through the Jellyfin proxy endpoint.

### Identity & Access Command Center
- OTP codes are no longer persisted in plugin configuration after the OTP flow.
- Login/password and OTP sign-in clear stored OTP state.
- The token box is masked by default, with explicit reveal/copy actions.
- Auth logs no longer include the login e-mail address.

### Operational Reliability
- Scheduled tasks now rethrow failures after logging so Jellyfin can mark task execution accurately.
- Cancellation flows are preserved instead of being swallowed as generic failures.
- AniLiberty progress pull no longer overwrites newer local Jellyfin playback positions with older remote timecodes.
- Clearing UI logs now persists the cleared state.

### Presentation & Documentation
- README now presents the plugin as a coherent product system: Signal Acquisition Layer, Context-Aware Reconstruction Core, Playback Proxy Rail, Mirror Governance Layer, Operational Command Center, and Distribution Quality Gates.
- Added three README visual assets showing the reconstruction core, system capability layers, and operational command center.

### Test Coverage
- Added tests for Jellyfin package pins and lock-file resolution.
- Added User-Agent and named/static HTTP client coverage.
- Added managed mirror tests for baseline creation, generated metadata refresh, unmarked NFO preservation, dry-run cleanup, delete cleanup, and empty-directory cleanup.
- Added proxy tests for streaming segments, playlist rewriting, unsupported upstream rejection, redirect validation, and upstream failure status.
- Added auth/config tests for OTP payload boundaries, safe defaults, and AniLiberty identity.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build in this release.
- No migration of AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.
- No destructive cleanup unless `StaleCleanupMode` is explicitly changed to `Delete`.

# AniLiberty API v1 Alignment, Better Metadata & Quieter Logs

This update improves AniLiberty authentication reliability, aligns the plugin with AniLiberty API v1 responses, and enhances generated metadata while keeping UI logs under control.

## Authentication & OTP
- Improved login and OTP endpoints with proper HTTP status codes and safer request validation.
- Updated OTP parsing to support the API v1 format (`otp.code`) and kept backward compatibility for older responses.
- OTP flow in the settings UI is simplified to **Start → Sign In** (the “Accept OTP” UI action was removed).

## Networking reliability
- Switched API calls to a reusable, DI-managed `HttpClient` (`IHttpClientFactory`) with consistent headers (User-Agent / Accept / Accept-Language).
- Added retry handling for rate limits (**HTTP 429**) and transient errors.
- Optimized HTTP reads using `ResponseHeadersRead` to reduce overhead and improve responsiveness.

## STRM generation & metadata quality
- Better year handling for AniLiberty v1 (`release.year` instead of `season.year`), including TV show year selection across grouped seasons.
- More accurate content classification:
  - Detects **MOVIE** by API `type.value` when available.
  - Routes **SPECIAL / OVA / OAD** into **Season 00** more reliably.
- Improved image handling:
  - Supports v1 image schema (`preview/thumbnail/optimized`) and prefers non-optimized URLs when possible.
  - Normalizes `.webp` URLs to `.jpg` and safely determines thumbnail file extensions even when URLs contain query parameters.
- Episode NFO improvements:
  - Writes episode titles (RU/EN when available), runtime, year, and sets `lockdata=false`.

## Logging & settings
- Added **“Enable debug logs (very noisy)”** setting:
  - When OFF: DEBUG/TRACE aren’t stored in UI logs and per-title progress logging is throttled to avoid bloating the UI log.
- UI log filtering now respects minimum log level and the debug toggle.

## Developer / maintenance
- Manual generation test is now **skipped by default** and uses environment variables (`ANI_TOKEN`, `ANI_OUTPUT_DIR`) so tokens aren’t stored in the repo.
- Internal null-safety improvements around plugin initialization.

## Not included
- No changes to library scanning behavior or broader UI redesign beyond the OTP/auth/logging settings shown above.

AnimeClick Metadata.overview: Metadati anime in italiano da AnimeClick.it, con setup guidato, vetrina, libreria a locandine e una comunità che condivide le correzioni degli abbinamenti. Solo per Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

versions.changelog: Corretto il doppio caricamento dopo un aggiornamento (issue #2): lo ZIP contiene un meta.json con il nome del plugin, così Jellyfin tiene tutte le versioni sotto lo stesso nome e rimuove la vecchia, e all'avvio il plugin segna come superate le proprie copie più vecchie. Licenza AGPLv3 con termini aggiuntivi (attribuzione, versioni modificate riconoscibili, marchi e mascotte); attribuzione e link al codice sorgente nella pagina del plugin. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AniList come fonte senza chiave insieme a TMDB: cast giapponese con i personaggi, studio di animazione, date, stato, voto, trailer, copertina e banner, solo nei campi vuoti. L'anno di una stagione senza date arriva dalla catena dei sequel di AniList, se gli episodi coincidono. Gli ID AniList che non corrispondono per tipo o anno vengono ignorati. Nuovo passo AniList nel setup. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Comunità per tutti: dopo una correzione il plugin chiede se condividerla e la invia tramite il servizio della comunità, senza account; il token GitHub diventa facoltativo. Si condividono anche le stagioni con una scheda propria, applicate agli altri solo se numero di stagione ed episodi coincidono. Elenco approvato aggiornato ogni giorno, controlli automatici e approvazione con un'etichetta, tessera Comunità in Inizio, passo Comunità nel setup e scelta della stagione in «Correggi un abbinamento». Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Pagina del plugin rifatta da zero con l'identità di AnimeClick: setup guidato al primo avvio e solo i passi nuovi dopo gli aggiornamenti importanti, vetrina degli ultimi anime aggiornati, cruscotto della collezione, libreria a locandine con titoli e trame uniti per anime, attivazione delle librerie a un clic e ricerca della scheda su AnimeClick per correggere un abbinamento. Corretti i conteggi dell'analisi di una singola serie, lo stato della condivisione comunitaria appena attivata e «Da verificare», che ora coincide con quanto «Sistema tutti i titoli» ricontrolla. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Scarta i titoli alternativi di un'altra stagione verificando il titolo inglese originale. Quando manca una fonte coerente, traduce il titolo inglese già valido; esclude i nomi dei file. Correzione trovata sul NAS in anteprima, senza salvare la proposta errata. Include le novità 1.2.1. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick come unico provider remoto per le librerie anime: identificazione TMDB verificata, completamento dei metadati senza altri plugin e immagini integrate Fanart → TMDB → AnimeClick. Chiavi Fanart personale e di progetto nelle impostazioni, con link e verifica. Numerazione, campi bloccati e immagini esistenti conservati. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick primo campo per campo: i valori generici lasciano spazio alle fonti configurate. Recupero italiano e traduzione dall’inglese anche per serie, film, generi e tag, senza mescolare titolo e trama. Le immagini conservano la precedenza dei provider ad alta risoluzione; nessun aggiornamento immagini o riparazione viene avviato dall’installazione. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Titoli episodio mancanti: ricerca su TheTVDB e TMDB configurati dopo AnimeClick, precedenza all’italiano e traduzione dei soli titoli inglesi con il profilo AI esistente. Verifica degli ID esterni, conservazione dei titoli compilati e indicazione della fonte nell’avanzamento. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

La tua libreria con analisi automatica, viste separate, avanzamento reale e interruzione dei lavori. Recupero dei soli titoli mancanti con protezione dei metadati esistenti. Abbinamenti della comunità e invio automatico delle correzioni su GitHub, entrambi facoltativi e disattivati di default. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Major per Jellyfin 12 e .NET 10, verificata su 12.0 e 12.1. Interfaccia riprogettata con guida iniziale, preferenze semplici e strumenti avanzati separati. Identificazione automatica più prudente fra titoli simili, remake e stagioni; correzione manuale cercando il titolo in libreria e incollando il link AnimeClick, senza cancellazione diretta delle immagini. Corretti redirect di rete, collisioni e scadenza della cache, concorrenza nei refresh, rate limit e coerenza della coda traduzioni. AI opzionale e disattivabile senza perdere il profilo; impostazioni e credenziali esistenti conservate. 210 test backend per versione server e 11 test browser. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo: non installare su 10.11; le release precedenti restano disponibili. Dettagli e limiti delle verifiche nel rapporto di audit della release.

Artwork Generator.description: Artwork Generator is a Jellyfin plugin that automatically creates custom episode posters using smart frame analysis, black frame detection, and configurable text styling. Perfect for filling in missing or generic episode artwork with clean, consistent visuals.

versions.changelog:
## Features
- Frames are no longer taken from inside media segments, so intros, credits, recaps, previews, and commercials stay out of generated artwork
- New Avoid Media Segments setting under Frame Extraction, with a checkbox for each kind of segment to avoid, all on by default
- Segments come from a media segment provider turned on for the library, so items without any extract as before

## Developer
- Changing which segments are avoided discards the idle frame pools, so the next refresh extracts under the new choice

## Features
- New Cleanup Backdrops scheduled task under Library that reduces every item on the server to a single backdrop, keeping the first and deleting the rest along with their files
- The task has no default schedule, so it only runs when started by hand or on a trigger you add

## Features
- Primary and thumb images can name a second and third design, adding their versions of the same frames to the Edit Images picker
- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes
- Edit Images reuses the choices it already rendered when switching image type or page, instead of rendering every image again

## Fixes
- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render
- Every design in one Edit Images render draws from the same frames, even while other items are extracting
- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Developer
- Settings saved before 12.0.2.0 are no longer brought forward, so update through 12.0.2.1 first when coming from an older version
- Code, pages, and docs say logo rather than series logo, since films draw their own

## Fixes
- The Profiles page loads again instead of failing on a backdrop setting that no longer exists
- Posters with a logo draw the logo selected for a film, season, or series instead of falling back to text

## Features
- Artwork Generator is Episode Poster Generator rebuilt, with the same settings and a much wider job
- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture
- Logo designs build a text logo from any name field, with letter case, a line limit, and frame-filled letters
- Frame extraction is one set of server settings instead of a copy on every design
- Frames are ranked on tone, detail, contrast, and color rather than just clearing a threshold
- Optional setting drops a subtitle that only repeats the title
- A subtitle too long to fit can shorten to its code, shrink, or trim
- Two example designs per style, each showing a genuinely different look

## Fixes
- Seasons extract from their own episodes instead of falling back to the series backdrop
- Candidate images come from different episodes instead of clustering in one
- Heavily letterboxed frames scale back up to a usable size
- Portrait text is measured against both sides, so it no longer reads small
- Brush strokes stay thick on tall posters instead of piling into a cross
- Long titles trim at a word boundary rather than mid-word
- Descenders stay inside the safe area
- Borders, rules, and shadows scale with the poster
- A static graphic keeps its proportions
- An item with no name of its own says its one line in the larger type
- Generated images carry the item's metadata language

## Developer
- The generator, the settings model, and the configuration page are rebuilt around item kinds rather than episodes
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 that Jellyfin 12.0 ships
- Designs are found by reflection, so adding one needs a class and an enum value
- Every label, option, and default is read from the settings models
- The shared generator is split into pipeline, text, and overlay
- Frame analysis is a single pass, under a megabyte per frame instead of three and a half
- Every one-time upgrade of an older configuration sits in its own file, to be deleted whole once installs have moved on
- Tests hold the documentation, the templates, and US spelling to the code

## Features
- Shadows, rules, and the Frame border now scale with the poster, so they read the same on a 4K frame as on a DVD rip instead of turning into a hairline or a slab
- Long titles that do not fit two lines fill the first line with whole words and trim only the second, at a word boundary, instead of cutting both lines mid-word

## Fixes
- Frame drew no border at all for an episode without a name, and ignored the Show Title setting
- Cutout no longer lets a two line title run into the bottom of the cutout letters
- Split center-crops the series poster into its panel instead of stretching artwork that is not 2:3
- Brush honours the Show Episode setting and keeps a wrapped title inside the area the strokes leave clear
- Timeline keeps the marker dot inside the safe area on the first and last episode
- Text blocks are reserved from the font's real ascent and descent, so descenders no longer hang past the safe area

## Developer
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 packages Jellyfin 12.0 ships, since the plugin binds to the server's copies at runtime
- Text drawing moved from the removed SKPaint text members to SKFont, wrapped in a shared TextStyle so every style measures and draws with the same objects
- Standard and Split share one text stack; Numeral, Cutout, Brush, and Frame no longer hand-build their own paints
- Cutout renders through a canvas layer instead of a full-size scratch bitmap per poster; Split and Brush dispose their gradient shaders
- Letterbox detection scans the pixel buffer directly instead of a native call per pixel
- Bitmap scaling uses explicit cubic resampling now that FilterQuality is gone

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Features
- Generated posters now appear in the episodes Edit Images dialog, so you can pick the frame you want instead of refreshing until you get a good one
- Choose how many alternate posters to offer in Edit Images, from 1 to 10 (default 3)
- Brush style can outline its stroke, sharing the Cutout styles outline toggle
- Element Spacing setting controls the gap between stacked poster elements, so every style spaces them the same way
- The font dropdown now lists the fonts actually installed on your server, and a font that is not installed is called out in the log instead of silently rendering in a substitute face
- Overlay colors collapse to an opacity control when Palette-Derived Colors is on, since the color itself comes from the image

## Breaking
- The scheduled task has been removed. Poster generation now runs entirely as a metadata provider - use a library metadata refresh, or pick a poster from Edit Images
- Processing history and its database have been removed, along with the Reset Processing History button. Jellyfins own refresh options now decide what gets regenerated

## Fixes
- Deleting an episode poster no longer left it permanently blank; there is no tracking state left to say the episode was already done
- Changing a custom font now takes effect; it used to be left out of the change detection entirely
- A tall logo no longer overlaps the episode code beneath it

Cinema Project.description: Every movie already has a soul: most of it buried in a poster and thumbnail. Cinema Project builds a virtual room experience around that instead. Walk through it like a video game: poster art lining the walls, a fanart and video slideshow across the backwall, theme songs filling the room, trailers, theme videos, or the movie itself playing on the screen up front. None of it is new, it's what your library already had, finally given space to be experienced all together, visualized all at once. On top of that, Ambient Mode lets you create your own feature show, similar to a pre-roll.
Cinema Project.overview: Watch and listen to the soul of a movie, a visualized experience you step into like a video game.

versions.changelog: Fixes the configuration page on Jellyfin 12, where **nothing worked**. Jellyfin 12 stopped accepting the older of its two ways of proving who you are, and the page was still using it — so every request it made was rejected before it reached the plugin. Libraries did not load, saved templates did not appear, the bundled fonts did not arrive, applying a cover did nothing, and opening the poster browser produced the cryptic message *"Failed to execute 'json' on 'Response': Unexpected end of JSON input"*, which was the rejection with no explanation attached. The page now identifies itself the same way the Jellyfin web client does, which works on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12 alike. **If you installed 4.0.0.0, update** — nothing was wrong with your settings or your covers, the page simply could not reach the server.

**Support for Jellyfin 12.** Jellyfin 12 moved to .NET 10 and changed its plugin ABI, so a plugin built for 10.11 cannot be built for both — this release is built against Jellyfin 12 and requires it. Nothing about designing or rendering covers has changed: your saved templates, applied covers and settings all carry over untouched. If you are **still on Jellyfin 10.11**, stay on **3.5.1.0** — your server will keep being offered that version and will not see this one, so nothing breaks by leaving it alone.

Fixes a small but confusing moment with **Live TV** targets. Live TV has no posters to build a mosaic from, so the **Poster collage** background is unavailable there — and if you had already chosen a collage and then switched the target to Live TV, the background silently changed back to **Image** without a word. The option is now greyed out with a line explaining why, in all three languages, so the change no longer happens behind your back. Nothing else about how covers render has changed.

Adds **Spanish**. The whole configuration page — every step, label, button, hint and message, plus the server's upload and validation errors — is now translated, joining English and Dutch. The page follows your Jellyfin display language, and regional variants come along for the ride: `es-MX` and `es-419` get Spanish just like `es-ES`. Alongside it, the translation files themselves were **cleaned up and put under test**. Roughly a hundred strings left behind by the v3 editor rewrite were still being carried (and would have had to be translated into every new language) — those are gone, and five new build-time checks now fail if a language drifts out of sync with English, if a `{0}` placeholder goes missing, or if a string is defined but never shown. No change to how covers look or render.

Adds an **overlay gradient** to the Background step — a colour that fades in over your background and sits under your text. It is the missing piece behind the look where a poster **resolves into a solid band of colour** at the bottom, with the title on top of it and readable no matter what the poster shows underneath. Each colour stop has its own **opacity**, so you can go from fully transparent to fully solid, use **two colours** for a duotone fade, or wash the whole cover. Four **presets** — Bottom fade, Top fade, Full wash and Duotone — get you there in one click, and switching between them keeps the colours you have already picked so you can try all four without losing your palette. The **Auto palette** swatches now recolour the selected overlay stop, so you can tint a cover with a colour taken straight out of its own artwork. The overlay works with every background type — image, poster collage, gradient or solid — and with animated covers. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The configuration page is now a **guided walkthrough**. Instead of every control at once, designing a cover is laid out as five numbered steps — **Target**, **Background**, **Text & logos**, **Effects**, **Output** — with one open at a time and any of them one click away. Each step shows the controls most people need and keeps the rest under **Advanced**. Choosing a background is now a single choice — **image, poster collage, gradient or solid colour** — instead of a source dropdown plus a separate gradient tick that overlapped with it. The whole page is **properly usable on a phone**: bigger touch targets throughout, the preview pinned at the top while you work, a full-screen poster browser, and canvas handles you can actually grab (they used to shrink to a few pixels on a small screen). Two more additions: **undo and redo** across the whole design with Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y, and an **in-context preview** showing your cover wide, square and poster-shaped before you apply it. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

Adds a new **Effects** card. A **colour wash** tints the background under your text, a **vignette** darkens the edges to draw the eye inward, **film grain** adds texture, and a **border** frames the cover — square or rounded, single or double-lined. Every effect is off until you switch it on, and turning one back down to zero leaves your cover exactly as it was. One click of **Jellyfin style** lays down the familiar dark-gradient look with clean white text, which you can then edit freely. And **Auto palette** reads the dominant colours straight out of your background and offers them as swatches — click one to recolour the selected text layer or the colour wash. Existing designs and saved templates are untouched and render exactly as before.

Covers are no longer one line of text. A new **Layers** card lets you stack **as many text layers as you like** plus your own **PNG logos and icons**, each independently styled and freely placed. Every layer can be **shown or hidden, reordered, duplicated, deleted** and selected from the list, and the card below it edits whichever layer you have selected. On the preview canvas, the selected layer gets **corner handles to resize it** and a **knob to rotate it** — hold **Shift** to keep a logo's proportions or snap rotation to 15°. Two new sliders, **Opacity** and **Rotation**, work on text and logos alike. Logos are uploaded the same way as backgrounds (PNG, transparency preserved) and are restored onto the canvas when you load a saved template. As always the server render stays authoritative, and rotated or faded text now renders there exactly as the preview shows it.

Fixes **Reposition background**, which barely worked in 3.0.0.0. Dragging the background now **follows your cursor exactly** — it used to lag badly at low zoom and overshoot at high zoom, matching the cursor only at one specific zoom level. More importantly, repositioning now **works straight away, without zooming in first**: on a **Fill** background you can slide a portrait poster up and down (or a wide still left and right) to choose which part of it the cover shows. Previously that did nothing at all until you zoomed in, because only the zoomed-in part of the image was treated as movable. The server render and the on-screen canvas were fixed together, so what you position is what gets applied. Designs you have already saved or applied are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The config page preview is now a **live interactive canvas**, not a static image: click the title to select it and **drag it** to position, and toggle **Reposition background** to **drag-pan** and **scroll/pinch-zoom** the background image directly on the canvas. A new **Show server render** button renders the exact same design on the server — the authoritative output, since the canvas is a fast approximation — so you can compare before applying. Designs are now stored internally in a new **layered document format** (title text is one layer, more layer types land in a later release); **existing saved templates migrate automatically** the first time you load them, so nothing is lost.

A code-quality and size pass. The plugin is now **much smaller** — the bundled Noto Sans fonts were subset to the glyphs cover titles use (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, punctuation), cutting the plugin DLL from ~3.9 MB to ~1.6 MB with no visible change. **Dead code was removed** (an unused retry service, an unused exceptions module, and nine internal API endpoints the UI never called), and the render pipeline was tidied up (the image compositing is no longer needlessly async). A few **security hardening** touches: the Apply and batch-apply endpoints are now rate-limited and batch size is capped, text size is clamped, poster-collage sources get the same decompression-bomb guard as other images, and error messages no longer echo server paths back to the browser. Purely internal — no user-facing behaviour changes.

Small UI fixes on the Target card: a **disabled button now clearly looks disabled** (dimmed, not-allowed cursor) — the Restore button no longer looks clickable when there's no backup yet — and the Restore row has proper spacing above it. Also added an animated preview to the README.

The **poster browser now covers every library type** — music albums and artists, books, music videos and photos, not just movies and shows — so you can pick a cover from a music or book library too. A **loading spinner** now shows over the preview while it renders, which helps for slower operations like building a poster collage. The **Apply** button now shows an "Applying…" state and locks while it works, so a slow render (like an animated GIF) no longer looks like nothing is happening. **Animated GIF covers are more reliable**: the working size is capped so a full-size render no longer takes forever or fails to apply, and text scales with it so the look is unchanged. The default **Landscape** size is now a lighter 1280×720 (it was 1920×1080) — plenty for library tiles and much smaller files; 1920 is still available via Custom. And the Templates and collage cards were tidied up — the **Delete** and **Shuffle** buttons now sit neatly next to their dropdowns instead of as oversized blocks.

Polish on the v2 release. The config page now matches Jellyfin more closely — compact colour pickers (they used to stretch the full width), and action buttons that align with the selects beside them. The preview no longer starts on a black canvas: it opens with Jellyfin's **brand gradient** (purple → blue) by default. And uploading an **animated GIF** as a background now animates the preview automatically — it switches to Animated GIF output and passes the source's frames through at their own timing, instead of showing a single still frame.

A big release. **Poster-collage backgrounds** build a grid mosaic from a target's own item posters (with density and shuffle controls). **Design templates** let you save a look and reuse it, and **batch apply** pushes one design onto many libraries, collections or playlists at once — each cover titled with its own target's name. **Animated GIF export** is now real: it passes through an animated-GIF background or applies a Ken Burns pan/zoom (capped at 30 frames). And **Restore original cover** reverts any target to its pre-plugin image — applying a cover now backs up the previous image automatically.

The plugin now has its own entry in the dashboard's left navigation menu, so you no longer have to open it through the Plugins list. Added **Live TV** as a cover target (best-effort — it sets the image on Jellyfin's generated Live TV view, which may not persist on every server). Moved the custom-font picker into the **Text** card where it belongs, and added a screenshot to the README.

Fixed the background dim: any non-zero dimming used to black out a picked poster entirely (JPEG posters have no alpha channel, so the overlay painted fully opaque). Dimming now composites correctly and the default was lowered to 0.25. Added an **Image fit** option — Fill (crop), Fit (show the whole image, letterboxed) or Stretch — so a portrait poster no longer gets cropped to a strip in a wide cover. New **multi-colour gradient** picker with an angle control for linear gradients and add/remove colour stops. You can now target **collections** and **playlists** in addition to libraries.

Poster background reliability: authenticate the image download, build the upload without the (sometimes unavailable) File constructor, and surface a clear message at each step so any failure is visible instead of silent.

Fixes. The config page now reliably follows your Jellyfin UI language — the detection reads Jellyfin's stored language setting, not just the browser language (Dutch now shows correctly). Picking a library poster as the background now works: the image is fetched through Jellyfin's own image endpoint and uploaded, instead of resolving a local file path that wasn't always available.

The config page now follows your Jellyfin UI language, with a complete Dutch (NL) translation and English fallback. Font weight now works — all six weights (Light–ExtraBold) are bundled as distinct Noto Sans faces. Background images are cover-fitted instead of stretched, so posters keep their aspect ratio. Added a Landscape 16:9 preset (now the default, best for library covers), a Download button for the generated image, and logging when a background image can't be used.

Redesigned the config page into a native Jellyfin two-column layout with grouped cards and a sticky **live preview** that updates automatically as you adjust settings (no more manual preview button). Styled the file pickers as native buttons showing the chosen file, and made allowed formats and size limits explicit. Fixed the empty library dropdown (libraries now come from GetVirtualFolders). Backfilled earlier version changelogs.

Bundled Noto Sans so titles always render (even on Docker/minimal Linux). Security & correctness hardening: fixed path-traversal and decompression-bomb risks, added rate limiting and font-signature validation, safe colour parsing, image disposal, and generated-file cleanup.
Initial release: custom library cover art with text, gradients, blur, custom backgrounds and fonts, a live preview, and a picker for existing library posters.

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10
Fix 3.2 build issues.

## Developer
- Server routes moved under the Allow system access toggle, so a page needs one permission instead of two
- Shortened the configuration page help text

## Features
- Allow local resource calls, so a page can define named server side routes and call them with serverFetch while the server forwards each to its configured target
- Optional per page Allow system access toggle that runs a page without the sandbox, so its scripts can call the Jellyfin API and reach other resources on this origin
- Pages on a signed in tier can now be restricted to named users, defaulting to all users at that tier

## Developer
- Defining a route also runs its page unsandboxed, since the helper cannot reach the route from an opaque origin
- A route credential stored before encryption existed is upgraded on the next save rather than left in the clear
- Route credentials are encrypted at rest and never sent to a browser, and the configuration page posts back a sentinel so an untouched field keeps the stored value
- Forwarded requests carry the caller's headers minus a deny list, so the viewer's Jellyfin session is never handed to a route target
- Route targets must be absolute http or https URLs fixed in configuration, so a page cannot turn a route into an open proxy
- A restricted page is refused before its body is rendered, so content never reaches a viewer the list does not name
- An allow list is refused on an anonymous page at save time, and fails closed at serve time if the stored list is unusable
- Pages stay sandboxed by default, and an unsandboxed page still reaches the browser HTML encoded inside the wrapper's srcdoc
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Developer
- Serve every page under one Content-Security-Policy so a page behaves the same at any visibility tier
- Allow pages to load external resources and submit forms, which the anonymous tier previously blocked
- Allow pages to be embedded by the Jellyfin origin (frame-ancestors 'self')
- Serve page HTML as UTF-8 so single-file documents without a charset meta tag render correctly
- Sign in correctly when the web client is signed in to more than one server
- Reject unknown visibility tiers and malformed asset content types when configuration is saved
- Key the decoded asset cache to the asset itself, closing a stale-bytes window around a save
- Keep unsaved page edits when switching pages in the dashboard
- Declare targetAbi 10.11.10.0 to match the Jellyfin packages the plugin is compiled against

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12

## Features
- Permission gate assets
- Documenation on calling a gated asset

## Fixes
- Enforce asset size cap

## Developer
- File cleanup

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a dns icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Fixed
- The plain-http warning no longer logs the request URL's authority, which carried the update secret into the server log for providers whose credential lives in the URL's userinfo (ClouDNS DynURL, Directnic gateway URL). The warning now names the record's hostname instead
- A Data Protection key store that fails for an unexpected reason surfaces instead of being silently downgraded to plaintext credential storage; the expected failures (bad path, no permission, no service) still fall back as before

## Developer
- Address the outstanding CodeQL findings across the plugin and test projects (LINQ filtering and projection, ternary assignment, dictionary lookup, response disposal in the HTTP test stub)

## Fixed
- Resolve the TTL "1 = automatic" sentinel to a per-provider default instead of sending a literal one-second TTL (Gandi, GoDaddy, Spaceship, Hetzner, DNSExit)
- Yandex matches records by type as well as name, so an IPv4 update can no longer overwrite an AAAA or TXT record, and A/AAAA now update independently
- Spaceship writes the new record before removing stale ones, so a failed update leaves the old address serving instead of deleting the record
- Hetzner treats an accepted, still-applying action as success instead of timing out and counting a false failure toward backoff
- DNS Made Easy treats "no update required" as success instead of walking a healthy record into backoff
- DDNS.fm validates the response body instead of treating any HTTP 200 as success
- NS1 record creation sends the required zone, domain, and type fields, so first-time setup works
- Apex hostnames infer the correct domain when no zone is set (Porkbun, Dynadot, Spaceship, Dinahosting), and Dinahosting gained an optional Zone field
- OVH DynHost, DynDNS v1, DSLReports, and NearlyFreeSpeech.NET declare IPv4-only, so an IPv6 address is no longer recorded as pushed and endlessly re-pushed
- A record with one working address family is no longer paused by backoff when only the other family fails

## Developer
- Harden the publish workflow (release body via env, tag-derived version, fail-fast asset downloads, required tag on manual dispatch)
- Slash-command dispatch uses the JF_BOT_TOKEN secret instead of a placeholder
- CI packages with build.sh and verifies the zip contents, and build.sh parses build.yaml colon- and space-safely
- Response-parsing tests for every provider plus orchestrator and API tests

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12
- Use ActivityLogger from Base 2026.7.12
- Use BackoffPolicy from Base 2026.7.12

## Feature
- Output logging to Activity Logs for better visibility

## Security
- Encrypt credentials saved through the generic plugin configuration endpoint instead of waiting for the next run
- Warn in the log when a record updates over plain http
- Show a dashboard warning when credential encryption is unavailable and secrets are stored in plaintext

## Developer
- Share one SecretProtector between the dashboard and generic save paths
- Snapshot the configuration per update run instead of mutating live records

## Fixes
- Prune record status against fresh record ids so a record added mid-run is not dropped

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.6.23
- Fix encryption of tokens to ensure they will not break between versions
- Migrate everything so it lives in the provider for ease of maintenance
- Reorganize files

## Documentation
- Creates Provider documentation per ddclient

## Fixes
- Check the DNS for current IP instead of always resending
- If the current DNS is internal, use the previous IP sent (previous behavior)

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.6.19
- Fix encryption of tokens to ensure they will not break between versions

## Fixes
- Remove URL from logging

## Initial release

This plugin acts as a DDNS resolver using Jellyfin as its host. A lot of this work will look very similar to [ddclient](https://github.com/ddclient/ddclient) which was a huge help and inspiration for this plugin. This takes the work they've taken and wraps it into a Jellyfin plugin for server owners don't want to manage more than one application.

versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.
